gloss: to bite; to snap at; to lash out at

definitions.gloss: to bite; to sink one's teeth into
definitions.explanation: To bite and hold on, especially said of animals. Describes an aggressive biting action rather than a gentle nibble.

definitions.gloss: to lash out at; to attack verbally; to snap at
definitions.explanation: To aggressively confront or criticize someone, often in an emotional or combative way. Used figuratively for verbal attacks.

examples.english: I was bitten by a dog.

examples.japanese: その{蛇|へび}は{近|ちか}づくと{噛|か}みつくので{注意|ちゅうい}してください。
examples.english: That snake will bite if you get close, so please be careful.

examples.japanese: {子犬|こいぬ}が{遊|あそ}んでいるうちに{手|て}に{噛|か}みついてきた。
examples.english: The puppy bit my hand while playing.

examples.japanese: {記者|きしゃ}が{大臣|だいじん}に{噛|か}みついた。
examples.english: The reporter lashed out at the minister.

examples.japanese: あの{議員|ぎいん}はいつも{野党|やとう}に{噛|か}みつかれている。
examples.english: That lawmaker is always being attacked by the opposition party.

examples.japanese: {上司|じょうし}の{意見|いけん}に{噛|か}みついたら、{会議|かいぎ}の{雰囲気|ふんいき}が{悪|わる}くなった。
examples.english: When I snapped at my boss's opinion, the mood of the meeting turned sour.

notes:
Compound of {噛|か}む (to bite) and つく (to attach, cling). The つく adds the nuance of latching on or holding fast after biting. Often written in kana as かみつく.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {犬|いぬ}に{噛|か}みつかれる: to be bitten by a dog
- {手|て}に{噛|か}みつく: to bite someone's hand
- {相手|あいて}に{噛|か}みつく: to lash out at one's opponent
- {噛|か}みつくように{言|い}う: to say bitingly

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {噛|か}む: to bite, chew — general biting without the nuance of latching on
- {食|く}いつく: to bite into — emphasizes gripping with the teeth; also used figuratively for showing keen interest
- {吠|ほ}える: to bark, howl — aggressive vocal behavior from an animal, but no physical contact

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {噛|か}みついていませんでした
